skill.name: seedance-v2
skill.description: Generate cinematic short-form videos with ByteDance Seedance 2.0 Pro through the local RunComfy CLI.
skill.summary: Use RunComfy to create Seedance 2.0 Pro video clips from text, image, video, and audio references.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are Markdown formatting false positives, including placeholder URLs and code-fence markers. Confirmed risks are the intended RunComfy CLI workflow, outbound RunComfy API submission, global CLI installation guidance, and disclosed token storage in a hidden config file. No prompt injection or deceptive override language was found.

remediation.issue: External CLI execution and network submission
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running RunComfy commands, and show the endpoint, prompt summary, reference URLs, and output directory first.
Pin or recommend a verified @runcomfy/cli version, and avoid automated global installs without explicit user approval.

remediation.issue: API token stored in a hidden home directory file
remediation.suggestion: Prefer RUNCOMFY_TOKEN for CI, document token revocation, and never read, print, or transmit the token outside RunComfy authentication.

remediation.issue: Third-party processing of prompts and media references
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to submit confidential prompts or private media URLs unless their RunComfy data handling policy permits it.

content.value_statement: Short video generation often needs clear model routing, schema details, and reference media guidance. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code prepare Seedance 2.0 Pro runs through RunComfy.
actual_capabilities: Routes explicit Seedance and ByteDance video requests to the Seedance 2.0 Pro endpoint.
Documents the RunComfy CLI command needed to submit Seedance 2.0 Pro jobs.
Explains supported input fields for prompts, image references, video references, audio references, duration, and resolution.
Gives prompting guidance for camera movement, identity references, audio tone, and lip-sync scenes.
Compares Seedance with related video models for common creative goals.
Lists relevant RunComfy CLI exit codes and privacy boundaries.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and an authenticated token.
The documented endpoint supports clips from 4 to 15 seconds only.
The documented playground resolution ceiling is 720p.
Video quality, identity consistency, and lip-sync accuracy still depend on the source media and prompt clarity.

use_cases.title: Create Short Product Ads
use_cases.description: Plan a short lip-synced product or spokesperson clip using a prompt and optional reference image.

use_cases.title: Prototype Cinematic Shots
use_cases.description: Turn shot language, reference media, and audio tone into a RunComfy Seedance generation plan.

use_cases.title: Automate Model Runs
use_cases.description: Use the documented schema and exit codes to integrate Seedance jobs into a controlled workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Text-Only Clip
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with no reference files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a five-second Seedance clip from this idea: [describe scene]. Use 9:16, 720p, and include natural ambient audio.

prompt_templates.title: Use an Image Reference
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for identity or product consistency.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Seedance prompt using this image reference for stable identity: [image URL]. The action should be: [scene action].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Lip-Synced Ad
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Seedance 2.0 Pro run for a lip-synced ad. The speaker says: [dialogue]. Use this tone: [tone].

prompt_templates.title: Combine Multiple References
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with image, video, and audio references.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a multimodal Seedance run with these references: image [URL], video [URL], audio [URL]. Preserve identity, scene motion, and voice mood.

output_examples.input: A cafe owner wants a vertical eight-second clip with a barista announcing a special.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Seedance 2.0 Pro, a 9:16 aspect ratio, an eight-second duration, a barista reference image, and warm conversational audio.

output_examples.input: A filmmaker wants a short previs shot from a still image, room video, and voice reference.
output_examples.output: The skill organizes the image, video, and audio references, then frames a concise cinematic prompt for a RunComfy submission.

output_examples.input: A developer asks why a Seedance job failed with exit code 75.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies the exit code as retryable, such as timeout or rate limit, and suggests retry handling.

best_practices: Use image references for stable identity, logos, products, and costumes.
Keep motion, camera, lighting, and mood directions in plain language.
Confirm the output directory and external media URLs before running the CLI.
anti_patterns: Do not describe a stable face only in text when an image reference is available.
Do not mix conflicting visual styles in the same reference set.
Do not request clips longer than 15 seconds from this endpoint.

faq.question: Does this skill generate video locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the local RunComfy CLI to submit jobs to the RunComfy Model API.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it use reference media?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents image, video, and audio reference fields for Seedance 2.0 Pro.

faq.question: What clip length does it support?
faq.answer: The documented endpoint supports whole-second durations from 4 to 15 seconds.

faq.question: Does it require authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires a RunComfy account and either CLI login or a RUNCOMFY_TOKEN environment variable.

faq.question: Are user prompts sent to a third party?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill states that prompts and referenced media URLs are processed through RunComfy model infrastructure.
